## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mTLS-based tenant isolation in CNF gateways, leveraging per-tenant ConfigMaps and a small sidecar to influence gateway TLS without full reconfiguration.

## Key Concepts
- mTLS in multi-tenant CNF environments
- Per-tenant CA bundles stored in ConfigMaps
- Sidecar-driven TLS configuration and tenant mapping
- Certificate CN mapping to Kubernetes namespaces

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-ca
data:
  ca.pem: |-
    -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
    ... tenant-a CA bundle ...
    -----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

```bash
# Generate a sample client cert for tenant-a (simplified)
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout tenant-a.key -out tenant-a.crt -days 365 -nodes -subj "/CN=tenant-a-client"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-client-cert
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  tls.crt: <base64-encoded-tenant-a-client.crt>
  tls.key: <base64-encoded-tenant-a-client.key>
```

- How would you rotate per-tenant CAs without downtime?
- How would you monitor and alert on TLS handshake failures per tenant?

## Why This Is Asked
Evaluates real-world CNF governance under multi-region and partition scenarios, focusing on provenance, attestation, and policy enforcement using Sigstore, SBOM, Kyverno/OPA, and distributed consistency.

## Key Concepts

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-attestation-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:

      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]

        metadata.annotations.attestationDigest: "*"
        metadata.annotations.sbomDigest: "*"
```

- What metrics and dashboards would you expose to detect drift between regional verifiers and the central ledger?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to implement tenant-scoped security policies inside a CNF gateway, using Kubernetes ConfigMaps for policy storage and a sidecar for real-time evaluation. It also checks understanding of config reloads and per-request performance.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-aware policy evaluation and path/method matching
- Sidecar design and ConfigMap-driven policy
- In-memory policy cache and reload semantics
- Path normalization and wildcard handling

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo: evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) -> boolean
function evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) {
  const rules = policy[tenant] || []
  for (const r of rules) {
    if (r.method === method && (r.path === path || matches(r.path, path))) return true
  }
  return false
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle overlapping rules or wildcard policies across tenants?
- How would you audit and rotate policies without downtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses real-world upgrade discipline in cloud-native networking functions (CNF): zero-downtime deployments, per-tenant TLS key rotation, and reliable KMS-backed certificate flows—all in a multi-tenant Kubernetes environment.

## Key Concepts
- Canary rollouts with per-namespace traffic control using progressive traffic shifting
- CSR-based TLS rotation via an in-cluster KMS-backed Certificate Authority
- TenantRotation CRD to trigger cross-namespace certificate refresh
- Readiness probes with TLS handshake validation during upgrades
- Traffic shadows for testing new versions without affecting production

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```


## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates advanced telemetry architecture, per-tenant observability, dynamic sampling strategies, and operational safety practices for CNF gateways at scale.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry, OTLP, trace context propagation, and baggage
- Namespace-scoped configuration and feature flags
- Adaptive sampling policies with latency-aware thresholds
- Canary rollouts and rollback safety

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.trace
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.trace.enabled: "true"
  cnf.trace.sample-rate: "0.25"
  cnf.trace.target: "otel-collector.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local:4317"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cnf-gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        env:
        - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: cnf.trace
              key: cnf.trace.target
      - name: otel-collector
        image: otel/collector:latest
        args: ["--config=/etc/otel/config.yaml"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: otel-config
          mountPath: /etc/otel
      volumes:
      - name: otel-config
        configMap:
          name: otel-collector-config
```

## Adaptive Sampling Implementation
```go
func AdaptiveSampler(sampleRate float64, errorRate float64) float64 {
    baseRate := sampleRate
    if errorRate > 0.05 {
        return min(1.0, baseRate*2)
    }
    return baseRate
}
```

## Rollout Strategy
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 5
      - pause: {duration: 5m}
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: error-rate-check
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        failedRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy-as-code proficiency, practical use of Gatekeeper/OPA, and ability to derive concrete manifests and validation steps for a CNF multi-tenant setup.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, hostNetwork, and Privileged security controls
- Namespace-scoped policy targeting CNFs
- Lightweight test manifests to validate allow/deny paths

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: cnfnamespacesecurity.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: cnf-a-security
spec:
  namespace: cnf-a
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-cnf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      privileged: false
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# Non-compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-cnf
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      privileged: true
```

## Follow-up Steps

- Apply ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, and test manifests in a single namespace and observe denial events for non-compliant pods.
- Extend with a quick kubectl patch to simulate remediation and re-validate.
